layman_headline: Solana position is green but the broader market is cooling — patience is the play.
layman_explanation: We already own Solana and it's up about 2.5% from our entry. The broader crypto market just dipped today with Bitcoin falling below $78K and ETF inflows breaking their 9-day streak. The swing trade candidates on the watchlist are either overbought (PUMP with RSI at 84), stablecoins with no upside, or gold tokens that are declining. There's no compelling new entry right now.
layman_action: Hold your current Solana position and wait. The stop-loss at $92 protects the downside, and the $115 target gives solid upside. Don't chase anything new in this dip — better setups should emerge in the next few days.
expert_reasoning: The current swing candidates are weak. PUMP has an RSI of 84 — deeply overbought and a correction trap. XAUT and PAXG are gold-pegged tokens declining nearly 3% on the week, offering no swing trade edge. MON (RSI 65) lacks volume data and MACD confirmation. The remaining candidates are stablecoins. Our SOL position benefits from the just-passed disinflation vote (supply reduction catalyst) and strong 7-day momentum (+11.5%). BTC dominance at 59.5% is headwind for alts, but SOL has been outperforming despite this. The Fed's hawkish Jackson Hole commentary ('work to do on inflation') and BTC ETF outflows create near-term risk, making it prudent to hold rather than add exposure.
risk_factors: Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish inflation comments at Jackson Hole could pressure risk assets further over the weekend
Bitcoin ETF 9-day inflow streak just broke — if BTC sells off harder, SOL will follow despite its own catalysts
SOL is up 11.5% in 7 days and may be extended; a pullback toward $95-98 is possible before continuation
watch_list: BTC price action around $77K support — a breakdown below $75K would warrant tightening SOL stop-loss
SOL reaction to the disinflation vote over the next 48 hours — sustained buying confirms bullish thesis
Fear & Greed index trend — dropped from 73 to 68, further decline toward 50 could signal broader risk-off
market_context: The market is in a mild pullback with BTC down 2.5% today, ETF inflows breaking their streak, and the Fed maintaining hawkish tone at Jackson Hole. BTC dominance at 59.5% continues to pressure altcoins, though select alts like SOL are outperforming on project-specific catalysts.
context_banner: Market cooling after a 9-day ETF inflow streak snapped — hold existing winners and wait for better entries.

key_signals.description: Solana validators approved accelerated disinflation proposal, reducing future SOL supply growth — structurally bullish for our existing position.
Fear & Greed dropped from 73 to 68 (still Greed), signaling cooling momentum — not ideal for new entries but not alarming for existing holds.
Bitcoin ETFs ended their 9-day inflow streak as BTC dipped below $78K, removing a key short-term demand driver.
PUMP RSI at 84 is deeply overbought, eliminating it as a viable entry. Other candidates lack RSI data or show no edge.
Fed Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole signaled more work needed on inflation, creating headwinds for risk assets including crypto.
